jobs.title: Data & Analytics leader
jobs.description:
Inclusion without Exception
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is an equal opportunity employer, and embraces diversity in race, nationality, ethnicity, gender, age, physical ability, neurodiversity, and sexual orientation, to create a workforce that reflects the societies we operate in. Our continued commitment to Culture and Diversity is reflected in our people stories across our workforce and implemented through equitable workplace policies and processes.
TCS is an IT services, consulting, and business solutions organization that has been partnering with many of the world’s largest businesses in their transformation journeys for over 55 years. Its consulting-led, cognitive-powered portfolio of business, technology, and engineering services and solutions is delivered through its unique Location Independent Agile™ delivery model, recognized as a benchmark of excellence in software development. A part of the Tata group, India's largest multinational business group, TCS operates in 55 countries and employs over 607,000 highly skilled individuals, including more than 10,000 in Canada. The company generated consolidated revenues of US $30 billion in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, and is listed on the BSE and the NSE in India. TCS' proactive stance on climate change and award-winning work with communities across the world have earned it a place in leading sustainability indices such as the MSCI Global Sustainability Index and the FTSE4Good Emerging Index.

The opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Data & Analytics Leader to help shape and grow enterprise transformation programs across the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance sector. This role brings together data strategy, analytics, AI, consulting, business development, executive advisory, and delivery leadership. You will work with senior client stakeholders to define transformation priorities, shape large-scale opportunities, and guide teams from strategy through measurable value realization.

What you will do

Build trusted relationships with CDOs, CIOs, CAIOs, business executives, and senior technology leaders.
Advise BFSI clients on enterprise data strategy, analytics transformation, AI adoption, governance, modernization, and operating models.
Translate complex business challenges into practical transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Lead executive workshops, discovery sessions, steering committee discussions, and strategic client conversations.
Drive growth for Data, Analytics, and AI services from opportunity identification and qualification through proposal, negotiation, and closure.
Shape large consulting and transformation engagements, including solution direction, value proposition, commercial approach, and delivery roadmap.
Lead RFPs and proactive proposals, ensuring solutions are differentiated, feasible, and focused on business outcomes.
Build joint opportunities with account teams, alliance partners, technology providers, and consulting practices.
Define target-state strategies across cloud data platforms, data products, analytics, AI/ML, GenAI, governance, and responsible AI.
Provide executive oversight from opportunity shaping and mobilization through delivery, governance, and value realization.
Lead and mentor consulting, architecture, engineering, analytics, and AI teams across locations.
Develop reusable offerings, reference architectures, case studies, estimators, executive narratives, and delivery playbooks.

What you bring

18+ years of experience across data, analytics, AI, consulting, and enterprise transformation, including leadership of large-scale programs.
Deep expertise in enterprise data strategy, data architecture, governance, operating models, data products, and data modernization.
Strong understanding of data engineering, including ETL/ELT, integration, APIs, orchestration, data quality, observability, DataOps, and platform engineering.
Experience leading analytics and BI initiatives, including enterprise reporting, self-service analytics, semantic layers, advanced analytics, and decision intelligence.
Knowledge of AI, machine learning, Generative AI, Agentic AI, MLOps/LLMOps, responsible AI, and AI-led business transformation.
Experience defining enterprise solutions across Azure, AWS, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake, and other modern data platforms.
Strong knowledge of BFSI requirements, including regulatory compliance, privacy, security, resilience, auditability, and risk management.
Proven success in consulting, business development, presales, solutioning, opportunity qualification, proposals, pricing support, and executive stakeholder management.
Ability to lead global, cross-functional teams and engage effectively with CXOs and senior business leaders.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline. A master's degree, MBA, and relevant cloud, architecture, data, analytics, AI, or program certifications are preferred.

TCS does not use artificial intelligence tools for candidate screening or evaluation. This post is for a current vacancy. The hiring process includes an initial screening, followed by a technical evaluation and managerial discussion.

Tata Consultancy Services Canada Inc. is committed to meeting the accessibility needs of all individuals in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code (OHRC). Should you require accommodation during the recruitment and selection process, please inform Human Resources.
Thank you for your interest in TCS. Candidates that meet the qualifications for this position will be contacted within a 2-week period. We invite you to continue to apply for other opportunities that match your profile.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Enersul L.P.

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

General Overview

The Director of Finance will provide strategic financial leadership to enable the company to grow responsibly, in a profitable and sustainable manner. The Director will ensure the integrity of accounting information and accurate Marmon Standard Practice Instruction compliant financial statements through strong internal controls and accounting knowledge, reporting to the Vice President of Finance & Controller. This position will be a driver of data-based decision making through financial analysis, collaborating cross-functionally, disseminating financial information and knowledge.

The Director will lead the accounting department with four direct reports, and will work closely with the Enersul Management Team. The position is an in office role based out of the Enersul head office in Calgary, AB.

Overall Responsibilities

The list below highlights the essential job responsibilities but is not exhaustive.

Partner with business leaders to shape strategy and drive key business decisions, leveraging financial and operational insights to identify opportunities, manage risk, improve profitability, and support sustainable growth.
Proactive management of month-end close, financial reporting, working capital, and account reconciliations, ensuring accurate, timely, and GAAP-compliant financial statements.
Lead budget and forecast preparation and reporting according to schedule, aligned with Marmon requirements.
Manage and prepare parent company reporting requirements through OneStream.
Ensure compliance with Marmon’s Standard Practice Instructions, Sarbanes Oxley internal controls, and Foreign Corrupt Practice Act. Ensure that financial and IT SOX documentation is maintained in a current manner. Coordinates and supports internal/external audits.
Coordinate and support annual and quarterly tax compliance, including the gathering, review, and reconciliation of information for income tax, sales/use tax, payroll tax, and other statutory filings, working closely with corporate tax and external advisors.
Properly disseminate appropriate financial data within Enersul and Marmon to aid corporate decision-making and planning.
Improve and implement new processes within the finance team to ensure continued improvement and innovation.
Manage the capital investment process (Authorization for Expenditure), working cross-functionally to assess payback and IRR, through to the accounting for capital assets.
Develop and coach employees to achieve maximum potential. Sustain a culture of innovation, high energy, and performance in line with Enersul’s mission, vision and values.
Contribute to other business priorities and projects as required.

Qualifications, Skills, Competencies

Knowledge of finance, accounting, budgeting and cost control principles including US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
ERP experience, Epicor or similar.
Knowledge of automated financial and accounting reporting systems and experience streamlining reporting for more efficient and effective results.
Operational business mindset, with proven leadership experience.
Self-motivated, organized, with strong attention to detail.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
CPA required.

Learn more about Enersul www.enersul.com

Following receipt of a conditional offer of employment, candidates will be required to complete additional job-related screening processes as permitted or required by applicable law.

jobs.title: Director, Indigenous Partnerships and Strategic Transformation
jobs.description:
We are honoured to once again be recognized as one of B.C.’s Top Employers.

If you are looking for an opportunity to contribute your experience, knowledge, and passion in a meaningful way, CLBC is the place for you!

Community Living British Columbia (CLBC) is a Crown corporation responsible for arranging supports and services for adults with developmental disabilities and their families. CLBC staff strive to advance the vision of Communities of belonging, lives with connection.

Term/Status:
Permanent, Full-time

Classification/Salary:
Management Band 6: Position starts at $139,562 to $174,453 annually

Team:
Indigenous Relations

Location:
Vancouver Head Office (hybrid – one day per week in office)

At CLBC, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We encourage applications from all people with relevant skills, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, racialized people, and those who identify as 2SLGBTQ2+IA. For accommodation needs, please contact CLBCPeopleServices@gov.bc.ca at any stage of the hiring process.

Visit our Careers at CLBC page to learn more about working at CLBC, what we offer, and tips for the interview process.

About The Opportunity

We are seeking a strategic, collaborative, and relationship-focused leader to join CLBC as our Director, Indigenous Partnerships and Strategic Transformation.

Reporting to the Vice President, Quality Services and Indigenous Relations, this senior leadership role offers an opportunity to influence how CLBC works in partnership with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities, while helping shape organizational policies, practices, and services to better reflect Indigenous rights, perspectives, and priorities.

The Director provides provincial leadership in advancing reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, and implementation of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (Declaration Act). Working closely with the Indigenous Advisory Committee, executive leadership, and partners across British Columbia, the Director leads CLBC’s Indigenous partnerships function and supports implementation of the Indigenous Advisory Committee’s Reconciliation Plan.

With responsibility for provincial Indigenous service planning, partnership development, contracting, contract management, funding arrangements, and placements, the Director brings together strategic leadership and practical implementation to strengthen relationships, support Indigenous-led approaches, and advance equitable access to culturally safe services.

This role offers the opportunity to influence meaningful organizational change, strengthen accountability, and contribute to improved services and outcomes for Indigenous adults with developmental disabilities and their families.

Key Responsibilities

Indigenous Partnerships and Service Development

Lead CLBC’s Indigenous Partnerships Strategy, building trusted, reciprocal relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples, Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities throughout British Columbia.
Work in partnership with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities to support Indigenous-led approaches to service design and delivery, strengthen Indigenous procurement and community capacity, and improve equitable access to culturally safe services.
Oversee provincial Indigenous service planning, contracting, contract management, placements, and partnership agreements, including alternative funding approaches with First Nations that support flexible, community-based service delivery.
Represent CLBC in provincial discussions and initiatives with Indigenous governments, ministries, Crown agencies, and sector partners.

Strategic Transformation, Policy and Performance

Lead organization-wide strategies and initiatives that advance reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, and implementation of the Declaration Act.
Provide expert strategic advice to executive leadership and the Board of Directors, guiding policies, governance frameworks, and organizational change that incorporate Indigenous perspectives into CLBC’s operations and decision-making.
Lead the development and implementation of provincial Indigenous strategies, corporate initiatives, and reconciliation action plans, including the Indigenous Advisory Committee’s Reconciliation Plan.
Establish performance measures and accountability frameworks to monitor progress, identify systemic barriers, and improve equitable access, service quality, and outcomes.

Indigenous Advisory Committee and Executive Governance

Provide strategic leadership and support to CLBC’s Indigenous Advisory Committee in fulfilling its legislative advisory role to the Board of Directors.
Develop strategic reports, briefings, and recommendations for executive leadership, the Board, the Indigenous Advisory Committee, and government.
Collaborate across CLBC and with provincial Indigenous leadership and government partners to advance shared priorities and inform organizational decision-making.

People and Resource Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team, fostering collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and a respectful working environment.
Oversee significant budgets, contracts, and resources, including an overall budget allocation of approximately $15 million, ensuring effective stewardship and alignment with organizational priorities.
Contribute to organizational planning, risk management, and strategic initiatives that support CLBC’s vision, mission, and values.

What You’ll Bring

Master’s degree in Indigenous Studies, Public Administration, Business Administration, Human Services, Leadership, or a related field. A bachelor’s degree supplemented by significant directly related senior leadership experience may be considered equivalent.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressively senior leadership experience in Indigenous partnerships, reconciliation, public sector administration, organizational transformation, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing strategies, service models, or initiatives in collaboration with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities.
Experience leading complex organizational or system transformation, including strategic planning, policy development, governance, and organizational change.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing complex projects, budgets, contracts, or partnership agreements.
Experience working collaboratively across complex environments involving multiple governments, organizations, and community partners.
Extensive knowledge of Indigenous histories, rights, cultures, governance systems, legal traditions, and the distinct perspectives and priorities of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Peoples in British Columbia.
Extensive knowledge of the Declaration Act, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s Calls to Action, and approaches to advancing reconciliation, cultural safety, and addressing Indigenous-specific racism.
Knowledge of Indigenous engagement, partnership development, government-to-government relationships, and Indigenous-led approaches to service design and decision-making.
Knowledge of public sector governance, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, and organizational change management.
Knowledge of the Community Living Authority Act, the developmental disabilities service system in British Columbia, and the network of organizations providing supports and services to adults with developmental disabilities.
Knowledge of trauma-informed, person-centred, culturally safe, and equity-informed approaches to leadership, policy, and service delivery.
Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with Indigenous leaders, government representatives, community organizations, and senior executives.

We recognize that relevant skills and knowledge can be developed through a variety of professional, community, and lived experiences. We encourage applicants to demonstrate how their qualifications and experience align with the requirements of this role.

We’re Also Looking For

A demonstrated commitment to reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, continuous learning, and strengthening relationships with Indigenous Peoples and communities.
A respectful, collaborative, and culturally responsive approach to building trust, navigating different perspectives, and developing meaningful partnerships.
The ability to navigate ambiguity, complexity, and competing priorities while maintaining a clear strategic direction.
A leadership approach that supports collaboration, accountability, staff development, and a positive learning environment.
The ability to communicate complex and sensitive issues clearly and thoughtfully with diverse audiences.
Sound judgment, political acumen, and diplomacy when navigating sensitive matters and competing interests.
The ability to build alignment, influence decisions, and translate strategic priorities into meaningful action and measurable outcomes.
Experience in a public sector organization or similarly complex governance environment is considered an asset.

Benefits:
A rewarding career at CLBC comes with great benefits including

Employer-paid extended health and dental plan
A BC Public Service Pension plan with employer contributions
Generous vacation plus additional personal days
Paid maternity/parental/adoption leave
Life insurance, paid sick days, and, if needed, long-term disability
Wellness supports, including an Employee and Family Assistance Program
Professional development funds and resources to encourage continuous learning and skill development
Access to government discounts on travel, cell phone plans, and more

Additional Info

Pursuant to Section 42 of the BC Human Rights Code, preference may be given to Indigenous candidates who self-identify as First Nations, Métis, or Inuit and possess the required combination of education and experience.
CLBC is committed to equitable compensation. Recognizing that salary negotiation can create barriers for some candidates, we use an objective approach to determining starting salaries that supports equity and fairness.
The successful applicant will be required to complete a criminal record check.
This role requires travel throughout British Columbia, including occasional overnight travel to Indigenous communities, partner organizations, and CLBC offices.
Possession of a valid class 5 Drivers license and a clean Driver’s Abstract

Closing date: November 19, 2026

If your application is shortlisted, you’ll be invited to an interview where you’ll have the opportunity to share more about your experience. Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

This opportunity is open to applicants who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

For more information, or to apply now, you must go to the website below. Please DO NOT email your resume to us as we only accept applications through our website.

https://communitylivingbc.prevueaps.ca/jobs/31948-18680.html
